analyzed_vuln.description: `htmlParsePI` checks for a processing instruction start with `if ((RAW == '<') && (NXT(1) == '?'))` without first ensuring enough buffered input bytes are available. With crafted/truncated input near buffer boundaries, `NXT(1)` reads past the valid parser input and ASan reports a global-buffer-overflow (1-byte read). The bug is a missing bounds/availability guard before lookahead access macros, not a harness issue.
analyzed_vuln.conditions: Triggered via the html harness (`htmlReadMemory` -> `htmlParseDocument` -> `htmlParsePI`) when fuzzed document bytes cause parser state to invoke PI parsing at/near end-of-input (or exhausted buffer) such that lookahead `NXT(1)` is evaluated on insufficient data. The PoC drives parser control flow into `htmlParsePI` from the pre-content misc loop in `htmlParseDocument`; malformed PI/comment/doctypish prefixes and truncation make the unsafe lookahead execute and crash.
